title: 扎克伯格怎样向员工承认判断失误、宣布裁员（2022）
topic: 扎克伯格怎样向员工承认判断失误、宣布裁员（2022）

source.title: Mark Zuckerberg’s Message to Meta Employees
source.license: 原文按项目方确认的授权收录
source.context: 基于 Mark Zuckerberg 2022 年发给 Meta 员工的信；人数、比例、原因及支持细节均为当时公告内容。
paragraphs: Mark Zuckerberg just shared the following with Meta employees:

Today I’m sharing some of the most difficult changes we’ve made in Meta’s history. I’ve decided to reduce the size of our team by about 13% and let more than 11,000 of our talented employees go. We are also taking a number of additional steps to become a leaner and more efficient company by cutting discretionary spending and extending our hiring freeze through Q1.
I want to take accountability for these decisions and for how we got here. I know this is tough for everyone, and I’m especially sorry to those impacted.

At the start of Covid, the world rapidly moved online and the surge of e-commerce led to outsized revenue growth. Many people predicted this would be a permanent acceleration that would continue even after the pandemic ended. I did too, so I made the decision to significantly increase our investments. Unfortunately, this did not play out the way I expected. Not only has online commerce returned to prior trends, but the macroeconomic downturn, increased competition, and ads signal loss have caused our revenue to be much lower than I’d expected. I got this wrong, and I take responsibility for that.
translations: 扎克伯格刚刚向Meta员工分享了以下内容：
今天，我要宣布 Meta 历史上一些最艰难的调整。我决定将团队规模缩减约 13%，裁减超过 11,000 个岗位。我们还将采取其他措施，让公司运营更精简、高效，包括削减非必要支出，并将招聘冻结延长至第一季度。
我想为这些决定以及我们如何走到这一步承担责任。我知道这对每个人来说都很艰难，对于那些受到影响的人，我尤其感到抱歉。
新冠疫情初期，世界迅速转向线上，电商增长带来远超预期的收入。许多人认为，这种增长会永久加速，疫情结束后仍会持续。我当时也这么判断，因此决定大幅增加投资。遗憾的是，实际情况并非如此：线上消费已回归此前趋势，再加上宏观经济下行、竞争加剧和广告定向信号减少，收入远低于我的预期。这是我的判断失误，我愿意承担责任。
fullTextParagraphs: Mark Zuckerberg just shared the following with Meta employees:

Today I’m sharing some of the most difficult changes we’ve made in Meta’s history. I’ve decided to reduce the size of our team by about 13% and let more than 11,000 of our talented employees go. We are also taking a number of additional steps to become a leaner and more efficient company by cutting discretionary spending and extending our hiring freeze through Q1.
I want to take accountability for these decisions and for how we got here. I know this is tough for everyone, and I’m especially sorry to those impacted.

At the start of Covid, the world rapidly moved online and the surge of e-commerce led to outsized revenue growth. Many people predicted this would be a permanent acceleration that would continue even after the pandemic ended. I did too, so I made the decision to significantly increase our investments. Unfortunately, this did not play out the way I expected. Not only has online commerce returned to prior trends, but the macroeconomic downturn, increased competition, and ads signal loss have caused our revenue to be much lower than I’d expected. I got this wrong, and I take responsibility for that.

In this new environment, we need to become more capital efficient. We’ve shifted more of our resources onto a smaller number of high priority growth areas — like our AI discovery engine, our ads and business platforms, and our long-term vision for the metaverse. We’ve cut costs across our business, including scaling back budgets, reducing perks, and shrinking our real estate footprint. We’re restructuring teams to increase our efficiency. But these measures alone won’t bring our expenses in line with our revenue growth, so I’ve also made the hard decision to let people go.
There is no good way to do a layoff, but we hope to get all the relevant information to you as quickly as possible and then do whatever we can to support you through this.

Everyone will get an email soon letting you know what this layoff means for you. After that, every affected employee will have the opportunity to speak with someone to get their questions answered and join information sessions.
Some of the details in the US include:
Severance. We will pay 16 weeks of base pay plus two additional weeks for every year of service, with no cap.
PTO. We’ll pay for all remaining PTO time.
RSU vesting. Everyone impacted will receive their November 15, 2022 vesting.
Health insurance. We’ll cover the cost of healthcare for people and their families for six months.
Career services. We’ll provide three months of career support with an external vendor, including early access to unpublished job leads.

Immigration support. I know this is especially difficult if you’re here on a visa. There’s a notice period before termination and some visa grace periods, which means everyone will have time to make plans and work through their immigration status. We have dedicated immigration specialists to help guide you based on what you and your family need.
Outside the US, support will be similar, and we’ll follow up soon with separate processes that take into account local employment laws.

We made the decision to remove access to most Meta systems for people leaving today given the amount of access to sensitive information. But we’re keeping email addresses active throughout the day so everyone can say farewell.

While we’re making reductions in every organization across both Family of Apps and Reality Labs, some teams will be affected more than others. Recruiting will be disproportionately affected since we’re planning to hire fewer people next year. We’re also restructuring our business teams more substantially. This is not a reflection of the great work these groups have done, but what we need going forward. The leaders of each group will schedule time to discuss what this means for your team over the next couple of days.

The teammates who will be leaving us are talented and passionate, and have made an important impact on our company and community. Each of you have helped make Meta a success, and I’m grateful for it. I’m sure you’ll go on to do great work at other places.

I view layoffs as a last resort, so we decided to rein in other sources of cost before letting teammates go. Overall, this will add up to a meaningful cultural shift in how we operate. For example, as we shrink our real estate footprint, we’re transitioning to desk sharing for people who already spend most of their time outside the office. We’ll roll out more cost-cutting changes like this in the coming months.

We’re also extending our hiring freeze through Q1 with a small number of exceptions. I’m going to watch our business performance, operational efficiency, and other macroeconomic factors to determine whether and how much we should resume hiring at that point. This will give us the ability to control our cost structure in the event of a continued economic downturn. It will also put us on a path to achieve a more efficient cost structure than we outlined to investors recently.

I’m currently in the middle of a thorough review of our infrastructure spending. As we build our AI infrastructure, we’re focused on becoming even more efficient with our capacity. Our infrastructure will continue to be an important advantage for Meta, and I believe we can achieve this while spending less.

Fundamentally, we’re making all these changes for two reasons: our revenue outlook is lower than we expected at the beginning of this year, and we want to make sure we’re operating efficiently across both Family of Apps and Reality Labs.

This is a sad moment, and there’s no way around that. To those who are leaving, I want to thank you again for everything you’ve put into this place. We would not be where we are today without your hard work, and I’m grateful for your contributions.

To those who are staying, I know this is a difficult time for you too. Not only are we saying goodbye to people we’ve worked closely with, but many of you also feel uncertainty about the future. I want you to know that we’re making these decisions to make sure our future is strong.

I believe we are deeply underestimated as a company today. Billions of people use our services to connect, and our communities keep growing. Our core business is among the most profitable ever built with huge potential ahead. And we’re leading in developing the technology to define the future of social connection and the next computing platform. We do historically important work. I’m confident that if we work efficiently, we’ll come out of this downturn stronger and more resilient than ever.

We’ll share more on how we’ll operate as a streamlined organization to achieve our priorities in the weeks ahead. For now, I’ll say one more time how thankful I am to those of you who are leaving for everything you’ve done to advance our mission.

notes.phrase: Mark Zuckerberg just shared the following with Meta employees:
notes.meaning: 扎克伯格刚刚与Meta员工分享了以下内容：
notes.explain: 这是正式通知的开场白，表明这是一份官方声明
notes.example: The CEO just shared the following with all company staff regarding the new policy.

notes.phrase: reduce the size of our team by about 13%
notes.meaning: 将我们的团队规模缩减约13%
notes.explain: 委婉表达裁员的方式，使用百分比而非具体数字
notes.example: Due to budget constraints, we need to reduce the size of our team by approximately 10% in the next quarter.

notes.phrase: I want to take accountability for these decisions
notes.meaning: 我想为这些决策承担责任
notes.explain: 领导者主动承担责任的表达方式，展现担当
notes.example: As the project manager, I want to take accountability for the delay and present a revised timeline.

notes.phrase: I got this wrong, and I take responsibility for that.
notes.meaning: 我判断错了，我对此承担责任。
notes.explain: 直接承认错误并承担责任的简洁表达
notes.example: The marketing strategy didn't work as expected, and I got this wrong. I take full responsibility for the miscalculation.

scenario.title: Summarizing the decision and taking responsibility
english: A colleague asks what Mark Zuckerberg said about Meta’s 2022 workforce reduction and how he explained his own role in the decision.

The message announced a reduction of about 13%, affecting more than 11,000 employees. Zuckerberg said he took accountability and explained that he had expected the pandemic-era growth in online commerce to continue, but it did not.
You summarize the scale, acknowledge the stated mistake, and do not replace the source’s explanation with a different cause.
chinese: 一位同事问，Mark Zuckerberg 如何说明 Meta 2022 年的裁员规模，以及他怎样谈到自己在决策中的责任。
邮件宣布裁员约 13%，涉及 11,000 多名员工。Zuckerberg 表示自己承担责任，并解释他原以为疫情期间线上商业的增长会持续，但实际情况并非如此。
你概括规模和他承认的判断失误，不用其他原因替代原文解释。

firstAttempt.prompt: 请用英文概括 Zuckerberg 在 Meta 2022 年员工信中承认的判断失误，以及他如何承担责任并回应受影响员工。
firstAttempt.sample: He expected the surge in online commerce to continue, but it didn’t. He said, “I got this wrong,” took responsibility for that decision, and apologized to the employees affected.
firstAttempt.rationale: 先说清他当时的判断和实际结果，再看他如何承认错误、承担责任并回应受影响的人。

words.example: The company has decided to cut all discretionary spending until further notice.
words.translation: 公司已决定暂停所有可自由支配的开支，直至另行通知。
words.note: 指非必要的、可自由决定是否支出的费用，常用于企业成本控制语境

words.example: The tech startup experienced outsized growth in its first year of operation.
words.translation: 这家科技创业公司在运营的第一年实现了超常增长。
words.note: 形容远超预期的增长幅度，强调增长幅度之大

words.example: Many businesses are struggling due to the recent macroeconomic downturn.
words.translation: 由于最近的宏观经济下滑，许多企业都在艰难求生。
words.note: 指整个经济层面的下滑趋势，影响范围广泛

words.example: The platform's revenue dropped significantly due to ads signal loss from privacy changes.
words.translation: 由于隐私变化导致的广告信号损失，该平台的收入大幅下降。
words.note: 特指广告平台因用户隐私政策变化而导致的广告定向能力下降

words.example: Our company offers competitive benefits to attract and retain talented employees.
words.translation: 我们公司提供有竞争力的福利来吸引和留住有才华的员工。
words.note: 强调员工的专业能力和价值，是企业重要资产

words.example: The company has imposed a hiring freeze to reduce operational costs during the economic downturn.
words.translation: 为在经济下滑期间降低运营成本，该公司已实施招聘冻结。
words.note: 企业暂停招聘新员工的措施，通常用于成本控制或战略调整期

structure.original: Today I’m sharing some of the most difficult changes we’ve made in Meta’s history.
analysis: Today 是时间状语，表示说话的时间点
I'm sharing 是现在进行时，表示当前正在进行的动作
some of the most difficult changes 是宾语，其中some of表示部分，the most difficult是最高级修饰changes，we've made是定语从句修饰changes
structure.transfer: I expected the pilot to reduce support time, but the results were mixed. I should have checked with the team before expanding it.

rewrite.bad: The market changed. The project did not work, so we will move on.
rewrite.good: We expected the new support tool to reduce response times, but it didn’t. I got this wrong, and I take responsibility for that decision. I’m sorry to the teams affected by the change.
rewrite.translation: 我们原以为新客服工具能缩短回复时间，但实际并没有。我判断失误，愿意为这个决定承担责任。对于受到影响的团队，我表示歉意。
rewrite.pattern: We expected [result], but it didn’t happen. I got this wrong, and I take responsibility for [decision]. I’m sorry to [people affected].

cloze.prompt: We expected online sales to keep growing, but they ___ to previous levels.
cloze.why: 用实际结果说明原先预期没有实现。

cloze.prompt: I got this wrong, and I take ___ for that decision.
cloze.why: take responsibility for 表示为判断或决定承担责任。

cloze.prompt: I’m sorry to the teams ___ by the change.
cloze.why: affected by the change 指受到调整影响的团队。

dictation.text: Sarah, a department manager, needs to inform her team about reducing the team size by 15% due to unexpected market downturn in 2022.
dictation.label: 听写 1 · 模拟团队缩编沟通
dictation.why: 15% 和市场下行属于模拟场景；扎克伯格 2022 年员工信写的是约 13%、超过 11,000 人。

dictation.text: She faces the challenge of balancing transparency with maintaining team morale while adhering to company policy about not sharing financial details prematurely.
dictation.label: 听写 2 · 透明沟通与信息边界
dictation.why: 这段为模拟情境。原文重点是约 13%、超过 11,000 人，以及 CEO 承担决策责任。

apply.prompt: 概括 Meta 2022 年员工信中的裁员规模，并说明 CEO 如何承担责任。
apply.sample: Meta planned to reduce its workforce by about 13%, affecting more than 11,000 employees. Mark Zuckerberg took accountability for the decisions.

translationPractice.prompt: 我们原以为线上销售会继续增长，但它回到了之前的水平。
translationPractice.answer: We expected online sales to keep growing, but they returned to previous levels.

translationPractice.prompt: 我对发布预测判断错了，我愿意为这个决定承担责任。
translationPractice.answer: I got the launch forecast wrong, and I take responsibility for that decision.

translationPractice.prompt: 我对受到这项调整影响的团队表示歉意。
translationPractice.answer: I’m sorry to the teams affected by the change.

choice.prompt: （情景练习）一项产品投入没有达到原先预期，团队也受到决定影响。请选择一段能说明预期与结果、承认判断失误并回应受影响同事的话。
options: The market changed, so there was nothing we could do. Let’s move on.
We expected the pilot to reduce response times, but it didn’t. I got this wrong, and I take responsibility for that decision. I’m sorry to the teams affected by the change.
The pilot did not work. The team should have handled it better.
choice.why: 把预期、实际结果、负责人态度和对受影响团队的回应说清楚。

output.prompt: （情景练习）团队原以为新客服工具能缩短回复时间，但试点数据显示并没有改善。请用英文向团队说明预期与结果，承认判断失误，并向受影响的人表达歉意。
output.sample: We expected the new support tool to reduce response times, but it didn’t. I got this wrong, and I take responsibility for that decision. I’m sorry to the teams affected by the change.
check: 是否说出原先的预期和实际结果？
是否承认判断失误并承担责任？
是否回应受到影响的同事？
